the use of intravenous midazolam in pediatric dentistry is associated with an increase in adverse effects, including respiratory depression, compared with intravenous ketamine.
the use of a combination of oral midazolam and intravenous propofol for sedation in pediatric dental patients was associated with fewer adverse effects than the use of intravenous propofl alone.

the effects of the use of sedative and anesthetic techniques in pediatric dentistry.

there is no evidence of the efficacy of the use of intranasal midazolam as a sole agent for sedation in pediatric dentistry and that there is no conclusive evidence of the efficacy or safety of the use of midazolam in combination with other drugs in pediatric dental patients.

the use of a combination of oral midazolam and intravenous ketamine is a very safe technique for the administration of intravenous sedation to pediatric dentistry patients.
